records.text: Feminism was a CIA-sponsored psychological operation.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This was a CIA-sponsored psyop.

verification.notes: Declassified/archived material confirms that Gloria Steinem's Independent Research Service received CIA funding for Cold War youth-festival activity. That narrow fact does not establish that feminism as a whole was a CIA-sponsored psychological operation, so the broad accusation substantially outruns the evidence.

sources.title: CIA FOIA: CounterSpy notes on Steinem and the CIA
sources.relevance: Archives material describing Steinem's Independent Research Service as CIA-funded; it does not substantiate sponsorship of feminism as a whole.

records.text: The feminist protests Owens was discussing were sponsored by men in government.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: These protests were sponsored by men in government.

verification.notes: The transcript never identifies which protests, officials, funding vehicle, dates, or jurisdiction are meant. Searches around the adjacent Steinem/CIA claim found funding for a youth-festival organization, not evidence sufficient to verify this separate sweeping claim about feminist protests and men in government.

records.text: Women are more miserable than they have ever been.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Women are actually more miserable than they've ever been.

verification.notes: Long-run studies support an absolute and relative decline in women's reported happiness from the 1970s into the early 2000s. More recent synthesis finds the pattern is small, period-dependent, and not universal, so the all-time superlative 'more miserable than ever' is not established.

sources.title: NBER: The Paradox of Declining Female Happiness
sources.relevance: Supports a historical decline in reported female happiness across several datasets.

sources.title: Two paradoxes in women's well-being
sources.relevance: Recent review qualifies the trend as slight, concentrated in earlier decades, and not universal.

records.text: Girls begin speaking earlier than boys, and women speak more words than men throughout their lives.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: If you have a daughter and a son, you know this. Women start, girls start speaking faster and we will speak more words from men for the rest of our lives.

verification.notes: Research supports modest earlier language development among girls on average, but the lifetime word-count claim is overbroad. A large 2025 analysis found women spoke more only from about ages 25-64; most other age groups were similar, and cross-linguistic child data do not show a universal sex difference.

sources.title: University of Arizona: Study determining whether women truly talk more than men
sources.relevance: Finds a word-count difference only for ages 25-64, not throughout life.

sources.title: Sex differences in language first appear in gesture
sources.relevance: Supports average earlier language-combination development in girls while not establishing a universal rule.

records.text: The ten women after the world's richest woman became rich because of whom they divorced.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And then the next 10 women who are the richest in the world are all rich because of who they divorced. Right.

verification.notes: Forbes's 2025 ranking directly contradicts the claim: nine of the ten richest women inherited fortunes, one was self-made with her husband, and only one top-ten entry's wealth estimate was principally tied to a divorce settlement. They were not all made rich by divorce.

sources.title: Forbes: The Richest Women in the World 2025
sources.relevance: Lists the top ten and their wealth sources, directly refuting the all-divorce claim.

records.text: Women do not have plenty of time to postpone family formation, biologically speaking, even if men might.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: You don't actually have plenty of time, biologically speaking, you literally don't have plenty of time. Men might have plenty of time, biologically speaking, but your body is telling you you don't.

verification.notes: The core warning is supported: female fertility declines with age and accelerates as egg number and quality fall. But male fertility also declines with age through sperm quality and quantity changes, so the contrast implying men may simply have plenty of biological time is too categorical.

sources.title: NICHD: Age-related factors in female and male infertility
sources.relevance: Explains age-related fertility decline in both females and males, with distinct mechanisms.
